summary: The historical runs reproduce exactly, but the experimental fit remains poor. The 32-start search returned 27 valid histories, three market-convergence failures and two timeouts, without improving the retained starting point. All eleven parameters were free; no differential-evolution or polishing round fit the time budget. Twenty-one local sensitivity histories and two exact repetitions then completed. This is a bounded search, not a fully optimized replacement calibration.
interpretation: The parent/nonparent ownership gap is the main problem: 0.44 percentage points in the model versus 16.77 points in the target, contributing 379.21 of the 450.71 objective. First-birth rooms rise by 0.365 versus the 0.720 target, and births occur too early. Smaller-shock starts improve ownership differences but worsen fertility fit. Other parameters also vary, so this is not an optimized trade-off or proof that simultaneous choice cannot fit the data.
outstanding: Resolve market clearing at the finite-grid affordability threshold and review the nesting restriction before another large search. The tested tenure nests require fertility taste dispersion to be no larger than tenure dispersion; simultaneous realization alone does not impose that restriction. All targets should be retained. The first-child room-floor jump has an upper bound of 2 rooms, versus 0.5 in the benchmark; high-income wealth reaches the upper plotted boundary. Production remains the presentation benchmark. Low-wealth conditional policies remain irregular despite passed occupied-state checks.
local_sensitivity: The 12-by-11 weighted local sensitivity matrix has numerical rank 11 and condition number about 1,271 in transformed parameter coordinates. The housing-supply normalization uses a one-sided difference because its negative perturbation failed market clearing. The weakest local direction is dominated by the bequest wealth-shift parameter. These finite differences do not establish global identification. Several unselected probes improve the objective slightly, confirming that the retained point is not a local optimum.
policy_interpretation: At this experimental vector, additional supply raises births by 0.93% initially and 2.83% in 2063; the mortgage policy raises them by 0.52% and 1.84%, with very small ownership changes. The large historical ownership miss limits these policy interpretations. Baseline adult-household mass falls to 71.18% of its 2023 level under the closed-entry experiment; this is not an empirical population forecast.
market_diagnostic: The tax branch fails at 2051, with residual 0.0002791 against the unchanged 0.0002 gate. A 72-price fixed-state trace finds a demand jump across prices only 8.19e-11 apart. Exact endpoint replays identify occupied renters switching from four to two rooms at the down-payment threshold. For wealth 0.4418605 and an 80% financed share, a four-room home becomes unaffordable above price 0.4418605 / (0.2 x 4) = 0.5523256. Both endpoints pass budget and value checks. This supports a finite-grid affordability discontinuity; it does not complete the tax path or establish economic nonexistence.
